items.title: 61427_Happy Caldwell oral history interview
items.q: on the Calvacade of Jazz We was at (Unintelligible) concert with Lips Page, and Conte Candoli and Charlie Ventura had (Unintelligible) and the other group

ctx.x: How much does tempo affect you? I mean, you know, if you were accustomed to playing a tune like you were playing on the -- at a certain tempo, and somebody hits it off much faster, I mean that changes what you play considerably, doesn't it?

Yes, it does, yeah. Changes the whole aspect of what you want to play, change it all the way around. I used to play (unintelligible) Body and Soul, three or four choruses as a ballad. Then we pick it up in two/four, fast two/four. But I quit doing it. Not that I didn't want to do it, but Charlie Ventura (unintelligible) tell me, he says, come here and listen. Said, why do you play it with the bell (unintelligible) play it in an even swing tempo? And so that's (the way) (unintelligible) wanted to do it. So I just…
Well, that's right. You can't help that. I mean that's impossible, but I think that there's another thing that has changed. You know those tempos used to be --
